chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants in His decree and judgment, but He is Just in that.
And he said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not create the Jinn and humans except to worship Him, and He did not create the Angels except for glorification and sanctification.
And he said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, created the Throne for His majesty, the Footstool for His grandeur, and the House (Kaaba) for His proof.
This is what has come in the book Kamal al-Din wa Itmam al-Niyyah in the hadith of the Number of the Shi'a.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological basis for Allah's justice in decree according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamal al-Din* underscores the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*) by linking the purpose of creation to the innate recognition of God, a concept central to the school of the Ahl al-Bayt. It contextualizes cosmic symbols like the Throne and Footstool not merely as physical entities but as manifestations of divine authority and order, reinforcing the metaphysical hierarchy established in Shia cosmology.
